Description: [New] The Reconciliation Preference field is visible on the patient payment plan and auto-populates to "No" (Do not reconcile) on a new plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with access to the Payment Plan screen; a new (unsaved) payment plan being created for Pat1; no reconciliation preference chosen by the user yet.
Test Data: Click Add to start a new payment plan for Pat1 and read the Reconciliation Preference field.
Expected Output: The Reconciliation Preference field is shown on the payment plan screen and is pre-filled with "No" / Do not reconcile without the user touching it.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan and click Add to start a new plan. 2. Locate the Reconciliation Preference field on the plan screen. 3. Assert the field is visible and enabled (not hidden behind another tab or section). 4. Assert its value is pre-filled as "No" / Do not reconcile. 5. Save the plan without changing the field. 6. Re-open the saved plan and assert the stored preference is still "No" / Do not reconcile. 7. Negative check: assert the user is never forced to pick a value before saving.

Description: [New] The Reconciliation Preference offers exactly three options: Do not reconcile, Reconcile to self/guarantor only, and Reconcile to family members balance.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient whose client setting "Patient Payment From" is set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only so the family option is available; Plan1 = a payment plan for Pat1 in edit mode.
Test Data: Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown on Plan1 and list its options.
Expected Output: The dropdown lists exactly three options — Do not reconcile (default), Reconcile to self / guarantor only, and Reconcile to family members balance — with no extra or obsolete option.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 in edit mode. 2. Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown. 3. Assert the option "Do not reconcile" is present and is the default. 4. Assert the option "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" is present. 5. Assert the option "Reconcile to family members balance" is present. 6. Assert the dropdown contains no fourth option. 7. Select each option in turn, save, re-open the plan and assert the selection is retained exactly.

Description: [New] Do not reconcile: the payment creates an Open Credit that is NOT applied to any balance.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = active payment plan for Pat1 with Reconciliation Preference = Do not reconcile; Amt1 = the installment amount charged; Bal1 = Pat1 outstanding balance before the charge.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 while the preference is Do not reconcile.
Expected Output: An Open Credit of Amt1 is created for Pat1 and remains fully unapplied; none of Pat1 outstanding charges is reduced and Bal1 is unchanged.
Verification Step: 1. Note Pat1 outstanding balance Bal1 and the open charges before the run. 2. Confirm Plan1 Reconciliation Preference is "Do not reconcile" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Open the Open Credit list for Pat1 and assert a new Open Credit of Amt1 exists. 5. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount equals Amt1 (fully unapplied). 6. Assert Pat1 outstanding balance is still Bal1 and no charge shows a new payment applied. 7. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler and assert the Open Credit is STILL unapplied because the preference is Do not reconcile.

Description: [New] Reconcile to self / guarantor only: the Open Credit is applied when the guarantor and the patient are the same person.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient who is their own guarantor (guarantor = patient); Pat1 has patient-responsible charges Chg1 and Chg2 with dates of service DOS1 earlier than DOS2; Plan1 = active payment plan for Pat1 with Reconciliation Preference = Reconcile to self / guarantor only; Amt1 = installment amount, large enough to cover Chg1.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 for self-guarantor Pat1, then run the Open Credit reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit created by the installment is auto-applied to Pat1 own outstanding patient-responsible charges, reducing Pat1 balance by the applied amount.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Pat1 is their own guarantor and note charges Chg1 (DOS1) and Chg2 (DOS2) with their patient-responsible amounts. 2. Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit is applied to Chg1 first (earliest DOS). 6. Assert Pat1 balance is reduced by the amount applied. 7. Assert only Pat1 own charges were touched and no other person balance changed.

Description: [New] Reconcile to self / guarantor only: nothing is reconciled when the guarantor is a different person from the patient.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient whose guarantor Gua1 is a DIFFERENT person; Pat1 and Gua1 both have outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = active payment plan for Pat1 with Reconciliation Preference = Reconcile to self / guarantor only; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 where Gua1 is not the same person as Pat1, then run the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: Because the self-only option reconciles only where guarantor and patient are the same, the Open Credit stays unapplied; neither Pat1 nor Gua1 balance is reduced.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Gua1 is a different person from Pat1 and note both outstanding balances. 2. Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the created Open Credit is still fully unapplied. 6. Assert Pat1 balance is unchanged. 7. Assert Gua1 balance is unchanged. 8. Negative check: assert no charge of any dependent of Gua1 was touched.

Description: [New] The "Reconcile to family members balance" option is available only when Patient Payment From is set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only.
Pre-requisite Data: Client setting "Patient Payment From" that can be set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only or to another value; Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 in edit mode.
Test Data: Set Patient Payment From to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only, open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown on Plan1.
Expected Output: With Patient Payment From set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only, the family option is offered in the Reconciliation Preference dropdown and can be selected and saved.
Verification Step: 1. Set the client setting "Patient Payment From" to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only. 2. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 in edit mode. 3. Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown. 4. Assert "Reconcile to family members balance" is listed and selectable. 5. Select it and save the plan. 6. Re-open Plan1 and assert the family option is retained. 7. Assert the other two options remain available alongside it.

Description: [New] The family reconciliation option is not available when Patient Payment From is not set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only.
Pre-requisite Data: Client setting "Patient Payment From" set to a value OTHER than Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only; Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 in edit mode.
Test Data: Set Patient Payment From to a value other than Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only and open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown.
Expected Output: The "Reconcile to family members balance" option is not offered (hidden or disabled); only Do not reconcile and Reconcile to self / guarantor only can be chosen.
Verification Step: 1. Set "Patient Payment From" to a value other than Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only. 2. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 in edit mode. 3. Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown. 4. Assert "Reconcile to family members balance" is not selectable (absent or greyed out). 5. Assert "Do not reconcile" and "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" are still available. 6. Save the plan with one of the available options and assert it saves without error. 7. Negative check: assert the family option cannot be forced in by re-opening or refreshing the screen.

Description: [New] Reconcile to family members balance: the Open Credit is applied across the guarantor and the dependents as allowed by the "Allow Payment From" client setting.
Pre-requisite Data: Client setting "Patient Payment From" = Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only; client setting parameter "Allow Payment From" = Immediate Family Members; Gua1 = guarantor with dependents Dep1 and Dep2; Pat1 = patient in that family with payment plan Plan1 set to Reconcile to family members balance; each family member has patient-responsible charges with different dates of service; Amt1 = installment amount large enough to cover more than one charge.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 in a guarantor/dependent family, then run the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit is auto-applied across the guarantor and dependent balances according to the "Allow Payment From: Guarantor Only or Immediate Family Members" setting, reducing the family outstanding balances.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm "Allow Payment From" is set to Immediate Family Members and note the outstanding patient-responsible charges of Gua1, Dep1 and Dep2. 2. Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to "Reconcile to family members balance" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit is applied to family charges and the applied total does not exceed Amt1. 6. Assert both guarantor and dependent charges are eligible for application (not only the patient own charges). 7. Assert each reduced charge shows the applied amount against the Open Credit. 8. Change "Allow Payment From" to Guarantor Only, repeat with a fresh Open Credit and assert only the guarantor charges are considered.

Description: [New] The user can change the Reconciliation Preference at any time, including in the middle of a running plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an ACTIVE payment plan Plan1 that has already had at least one successful installment; Plan1 Reconciliation Preference currently = Do not reconcile.
Test Data: Open the running plan Plan1 mid-schedule and change the Reconciliation Preference, then save.
Expected Output: The Reconciliation Preference stays editable even after the plan has run; the change saves successfully without being blocked by the post-first-transaction term lock.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 which already has at least one successful installment. 2. Assert the locked term fields (Plan Code, Amount, Frequency, Start Date) are read-only. 3. Assert the Reconciliation Preference field is still editable. 4. Change the preference to another option and save. 5. Assert the plan saves without any validation error. 6. Re-open Plan1 and assert the new preference is stored. 7. Change it a second time and assert it can be changed again with no limit on the number of changes.

Description: [New] A changed Reconciliation Preference applies to reconciliation performed after the change, not retrospectively to Open Credits already processed.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with outstanding patient-responsible charges and an active payment plan Plan1; Plan1 initially set to Do not reconcile; OC1 = the Open Credit created by an installment run while the preference was Do not reconcile; OC2 = the Open Credit created by the next installment after the preference is changed to a reconcile option.
Test Data: Run one installment with Do not reconcile, change the preference to a reconcile option, then run the next installment.
Expected Output: OC2 (created after the change) is auto-reconciled per the new preference; OC1 remains as it was left when it was processed under the old preference, so the change only drives subsequent reconciliation.
Verification Step: 1. With Plan1 set to Do not reconcile, run one installment and note the created Open Credit OC1 and its unapplied amount. 2. Run the Open Credit reconcile scheduler and assert OC1 stays unapplied. 3. Change Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to a reconcile option and save. 4. Run the next installment so Open Credit OC2 is created. 5. Run the reconcile scheduler again. 6. Assert OC2 is applied to the eligible balances per the new preference. 7. Assert the state of OC1 as previously processed is not retroactively altered by the preference change alone.

Description: [New] Switching the preference from a reconcile option back to Do not reconcile stops further automatic application.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = active payment plan currently set to a reconcile option and already auto-applying Open Credits; Bal1 = Pat1 outstanding balance at the moment of the switch.
Test Data: Switch Plan1 Reconciliation Preference from a reconcile option back to Do not reconcile, then run the next installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: After the switch, the Open Credit created by the next installment is left fully unapplied and Pat1 balance stays at Bal1 minus nothing; previously applied amounts are untouched.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Plan1 is set to a reconcile option and that an earlier installment was auto-applied. 2. Note Pat1 outstanding balance Bal1 and the already-applied Open Credits. 3. Change the Reconciliation Preference to "Do not reconcile" and save. 4. Run the next installment so a new Open Credit is created. 5. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 6. Assert the new Open Credit is fully unapplied. 7. Assert Pat1 outstanding balance is unchanged after the scheduler run. 8. Assert the previously applied Open Credits remain applied and are not reversed.

Description: [New] The chosen Reconciliation Preference is stored with the plan and survives reopening, refreshing and re-login.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1; Opt1 = any Reconciliation Preference option other than the default.
Test Data: Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to Opt1, save, then reopen after refresh and re-login.
Expected Output: The stored preference Opt1 is shown every time the plan is opened, and it is the value the reconciliation logic uses.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1, set Reconciliation Preference to Opt1 and save. 2. Close and re-open Plan1 and assert the field shows Opt1. 3. Refresh the browser, re-open Plan1 and assert it still shows Opt1. 4. Log out, log back in, re-open Plan1 and assert it still shows Opt1. 5. Open Plan1 from a different entry point (plan level tracking) and assert the same value is shown. 6. Assert the value is not reset to the default "No" on any of these paths.

Description: [New] Auto reconciliation applies the Open Credit to charges by Date of Service, earliest first.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient/guarantor family eligible for reconciliation under the chosen preference; Chg1, Chg2, Chg3 = outstanding patient-responsible charges with dates of service DOS1 < DOS2 < DOS3; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile preference; Amt1 = installment amount sufficient to cover Chg1 and Chg2 but not Chg3.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1 and run the Open Credit reconcile scheduler with three charges at different dates of service.
Expected Output: The Open Credit is applied first to the charge with the earliest DOS, then to the next earliest, until the credit is exhausted; the latest-DOS charge is left untouched.
Verification Step: 1. Note the outstanding patient-responsible charges Chg1 (DOS1), Chg2 (DOS2) and Chg3 (DOS3) in date-of-service order. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile preference and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert Chg1 is fully applied first. 6. Assert Chg2 is applied next with whatever credit remains. 7. Assert Chg3 (latest DOS) receives nothing because the credit is exhausted. 8. Assert the sum of all applied amounts equals exactly Amt1 or the credit available, never more.

Description: [New] Auto reconciliation follows pure Date of Service order with NO patient-first or guarantor-first priority.
Pre-requisite Data: Family with guarantor Gua1 and patient Pat1 eligible under the family reconcile preference; charges interleaved by DOS so that the earliest charge belongs to Gua1, the next to Pat1 and the next to Gua1 again; Plan1 = Pat1 payment plan set to reconcile to family members balance; Amt1 = installment amount covering the first two charges only.
Test Data: Create charges whose dates of service alternate between the guarantor and the patient, then run one installment and the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The credit is applied strictly in date-of-service order across the whole eligible group; the patient charges are not served before the guarantor charges (and vice versa) just because of who they belong to.
Verification Step: 1. Note the eligible outstanding charges in date-of-service order and record which person each belongs to (alternating guarantor/patient). 2. Set Plan1 to "Reconcile to family members balance" and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the earliest-DOS charge is applied first even though it belongs to the guarantor and not the patient. 6. Assert the second-earliest charge is applied next regardless of owner. 7. Negative check: assert no later-DOS charge was applied ahead of an earlier-DOS charge because of patient/guarantor priority. 8. Assert the applied sequence, read by DOS, is strictly ascending.

Description: [New] When reconciling a guarantor or dependent balance the system checks that the Date of Service falls inside that person from–to date range.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor linked to patient Pat1 with an effective from date From1 and to date To1; ChgIn = a patient-responsible charge whose DOS falls inside From1..To1; ChgOut = a charge whose DOS falls outside that range; Plan1 = payment plan set to a reconcile option that covers the guarantor/dependent; Amt1 = installment amount big enough to cover both charges.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 with one in-range charge and one out-of-range charge for the guarantor/dependent, then run the scheduler.
Expected Output: Only ChgIn, whose DOS falls inside the guarantor/dependent from–to range, is reconciled; ChgOut is skipped and the unused credit stays unapplied.
Verification Step: 1. Note the guarantor/dependent link from date From1 and to date To1 for Gua1 and Pat1. 2. Identify ChgIn (DOS inside the range) and ChgOut (DOS outside the range) with their patient-responsible amounts. 3. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 4. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert ChgIn is applied. 6. Assert ChgOut is NOT applied and still shows its full outstanding amount. 7. Assert the remaining credit stays on the Open Credit as unapplied rather than being forced onto ChgOut. 8. Assert no error is raised while skipping the out-of-range charge.

Description: [New] Charges whose Date of Service falls outside the guarantor/dependent from–to range are skipped and the next eligible charge is taken instead.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor with link range From1..To1; Chg1 = earliest-DOS charge but OUTSIDE the range; Chg2 = later-DOS charge INSIDE the range; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option covering the guarantor; Amt1 = installment amount covering one charge.
Test Data: Make the earliest-DOS charge fall outside the guarantor link range and the next charge inside it, then run the installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: The out-of-range earliest charge Chg1 is skipped entirely and the credit moves on to the next eligible in-range charge Chg2, still honouring DOS order among eligible charges.
Verification Step: 1. Note Chg1 (earliest DOS, outside From1..To1) and Chg2 (later DOS, inside the range). 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert Chg1 is untouched and still fully outstanding. 5. Assert Chg2 is applied instead. 6. Assert the applied amount does not exceed the patient-responsible amount of Chg2. 7. Assert the skip is silent (no failure of the whole reconcile run). 8. Assert re-running the scheduler does not later apply anything to Chg1.

Description: [New] Boundary: a charge whose Date of Service is exactly the guarantor/dependent FROM date is reconciled.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor/dependent link with from date From1 and to date To1; ChgFrom = a patient-responsible charge whose DOS equals From1 exactly; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option covering that person; Amt1 = installment amount covering ChgFrom.
Test Data: A charge dated exactly on the link from date; run one installment and the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The charge dated exactly on the from date is treated as inside the range and is reconciled — the range check is inclusive of the from date.
Verification Step: 1. Create/identify ChgFrom with DOS exactly equal to From1. 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert ChgFrom is applied and its outstanding amount is reduced. 6. Assert the Open Credit shows the corresponding applied amount against ChgFrom. 7. Negative check: create a charge dated one day BEFORE From1 and assert it is skipped.

Description: [New] Boundary: a charge whose Date of Service is exactly the guarantor/dependent TO date is reconciled.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor/dependent link with from date From1 and to date To1; ChgTo = a patient-responsible charge whose DOS equals To1 exactly; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option covering that person; Amt1 = installment amount covering ChgTo.
Test Data: A charge dated exactly on the link to date; run one installment and the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The charge dated exactly on the to date is treated as inside the range and is reconciled — the range check is inclusive of the to date.
Verification Step: 1. Create/identify ChgTo with DOS exactly equal to To1. 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert ChgTo is applied and its outstanding amount is reduced. 6. Assert the applied amount is recorded against the Open Credit. 7. Negative check: create a charge dated one day AFTER To1 and assert it is skipped and stays fully outstanding.

Description: [New] Only the patient-responsible amount is reconciled by auto reconciliation.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation; ChgMix = an outstanding charge split into a patient-responsible part PR1 and an insurance-pending part INS1; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount larger than PR1.
Test Data: A charge carrying both a patient-responsible portion and an insurance-pending portion; run one installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit is applied only up to the patient-responsible amount PR1 of the charge; the insurance-pending portion INS1 is left untouched and any remaining credit stays unapplied or moves to the next eligible patient-responsible charge.
Verification Step: 1. Note charge ChgMix with its patient-responsible amount PR1 and insurance-pending amount INS1. 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the amount applied to ChgMix equals PR1 and no more. 6. Assert the insurance-pending amount INS1 is unchanged on the charge. 7. Assert the leftover credit (Amt1 minus PR1) either moves to the next eligible patient-responsible charge or stays unapplied. 8. Assert the insurance balance total for Pat1 is unchanged.

Description: [New] An amount that is entirely pending with insurance is never reconciled by auto reconciliation.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation; ChgIns = an outstanding charge with the whole amount pending with insurance and zero patient responsibility; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: A charge fully pending with insurance and no other eligible patient-responsible charge; run one installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: Nothing is applied to the insurance-pending charge; the Open Credit remains fully unapplied and the insurance-pending amount stays exactly as it was.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm ChgIns has zero patient-responsible amount and the full amount pending with insurance. 2. Confirm no other eligible patient-responsible charge exists for the reconciliation scope. 3. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 4. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount is still Amt1. 6. Assert ChgIns shows no payment applied. 7. Assert the insurance-pending amount on ChgIns is unchanged. 8. Assert no error or stuck scheduler entry results from having nothing to apply.

Description: [New] Auto reconciliation is carried out by the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler can be viewed and run; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1 and observe the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler entry before and after the run.
Expected Output: The installment creates an Open Credit and an entry for the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler; the credit is applied to balances when that scheduler runs, not at the instant of the charge.
Verification Step: 1. Note Pat1 outstanding charges before the run. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Immediately check the balances and assert the Open Credit is created and queued for reconciliation. 5. Open the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler and assert an entry exists for this Open Credit. 6. Run the scheduler. 7. Assert the Open Credit is now applied to the eligible charges. 8. Assert the scheduler entry is completed and the same credit is not applied twice on a second run.

Description: [New] If the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler has not run, the Open Credit stays unapplied even when the preference is set to reconcile.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with eligible outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler is stopped/not yet due; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 with the reconcile scheduler not running, then inspect the balances.
Expected Output: The Open Credit exists and is unapplied until the scheduler runs; balances are only changed by the scheduler, never as an untracked side effect of the charge.
Verification Step: 1. Ensure the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler is stopped or not yet due. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Assert the Open Credit is created with the full amount unapplied. 5. Assert Pat1 outstanding charges are unchanged. 6. Start / run the scheduler. 7. Assert the Open Credit is then applied per the preference. 8. Assert nothing was applied before the scheduler ran.

Description: [New] Zero balance: when there is nothing outstanding to reconcile the Open Credit stays fully unapplied.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient (and, for the family option, a family) with a ZERO outstanding patient-responsible balance; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 while the eligible balance is zero, then run the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit of Amt1 is created and remains fully unapplied because there is no outstanding patient-responsible charge to apply it to; no negative balance is created.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm the eligible outstanding patient-responsible balance for the reconciliation scope is zero. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount equals Amt1. 6. Assert no charge shows a payment applied. 7. Assert no negative (credit) balance is created on any account. 8. Add a new patient-responsible charge, re-run the scheduler and assert the waiting credit is then applied to it.

Description: [New] Open Credit larger than the total outstanding balance: the leftover amount stays unapplied.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient/family eligible for reconciliation; TotBal1 = the total eligible outstanding patient-responsible balance; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount that is GREATER than TotBal1.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 where Amt1 is larger than the total eligible balance TotBal1, then run the scheduler.
Expected Output: All eligible charges are cleared to zero and the leftover (Amt1 minus TotBal1) remains on the Open Credit as an unapplied amount; it is never forced onto ineligible or insurance-pending charges.
Verification Step: 1. Note the total eligible outstanding patient-responsible balance TotBal1 and confirm Amt1 is greater than it. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert every eligible charge is reduced to zero outstanding. 5. Assert the Open Credit shows an unapplied amount equal to Amt1 minus TotBal1. 6. Assert no insurance-pending amount was consumed by the leftover. 7. Assert no charge is over-applied (no negative outstanding on any charge). 8. Add a new eligible charge, re-run the scheduler and assert the leftover is then applied to it.

Description: [New] Open Credit smaller than the earliest charge: the earliest-DOS charge is partially applied and the rest stays outstanding.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation; Chg1 = the earliest-DOS eligible charge with a patient-responsible amount LARGER than the installment amount; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount smaller than Chg1 patient-responsible amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 where Amt1 is smaller than the earliest eligible charge, then run the scheduler.
Expected Output: The whole credit Amt1 is applied to the earliest-DOS charge Chg1, which stays partly outstanding; no later charge receives anything and the Open Credit becomes fully applied.
Verification Step: 1. Note Chg1 as the earliest-DOS eligible charge and confirm its patient-responsible amount exceeds Amt1. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert the full Amt1 is applied to Chg1. 5. Assert Chg1 still shows the remaining outstanding difference. 6. Assert no later-DOS charge received any amount. 7. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount is now zero.

Description: [New] End-to-end: a successful plan charge creates an Open Credit that the scheduler applies to the earliest eligible balances per the chosen preference.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation with several outstanding patient-responsible charges at different dates of service; Plan1 = active payment plan with a reconcile option and card Card1; Amt1 = installment amount; Open Credit reconcile event scheduler available.
Test Data: Run the full cycle on Plan1: charge, Open Credit creation, scheduler run, balance update.
Expected Output: The charge succeeds, an Open Credit of the charge amount is created for Pat1, the reconcile scheduler applies it in DOS order to the eligible patient-responsible balances, and the patient statement/ledger reflects the reduced balances.
Verification Step: 1. Note the outstanding eligible charges of Pat1 in DOS order and the total balance. 2. Confirm Plan1 Reconciliation Preference is a reconcile option. 3. Run a successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 and confirm the receipt is created. 4. Assert an Open Credit of the collected amount exists for Pat1. 5. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 6. Assert the credit is applied in DOS order, earliest first. 7. Assert the total outstanding balance is reduced by exactly the applied amount. 8. Assert the ledger/statement view shows the applications against the correct charges.

Description: [New] Self / guarantor only: dependents balances are never touched even when the patient has nothing outstanding.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient who is their own guarantor with ZERO outstanding patient-responsible balance; Dep1 = a dependent of Pat1 with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = Pat1 payment plan set to Reconcile to self / guarantor only; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 under the self-only preference with the patient at zero balance and the dependent carrying a balance.
Expected Output: The dependent balance is not reconciled under the self / guarantor only option; the Open Credit stays unapplied even though the dependent owes money.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Pat1 (self-guarantor) has zero outstanding patient-responsible balance and Dep1 has outstanding charges. 2. Set Plan1 to "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert the Open Credit is still fully unapplied. 5. Assert Dep1 outstanding charges are unchanged. 6. Assert no application row is created against any dependent charge. 7. Switch Plan1 to the family option (where allowed), re-run the scheduler and assert the dependent charges then become eligible.
